verdict.rationale: Babylon.js has extensive first-party docs (llms.txt, TypeDoc, Playground with shareable examples), TypeScript IntelliSense, and community praise for documentation quality and strong backwards compatibility (comm-3, comm-5, comm-8) — all factors that favor LLM familiarity and code stability. However, there is no direct evidence of LLM-generated code success rates, and some community feedback flags API rough edges (e.g., physics API design criticized in comm-1, object-allocation/GC concerns in comm-12) that could trip up naive generated code. Missing for 10: direct evidence of LLM/AI code-generation success with Babylon.js, and confirmation that abundant training-data examples exist beyond the docs themselves.
